rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Class 12 ray optics unifies mirrors, refraction, TIR, prisms and lenses into instruments: the compound microscope stages two magnifications (objective makes a real enlarged image, eyepiece magnifies it as a loupe), while the astronomical telescope pairs a long-focus objective (light bucket) with a short eyepiece. Magnifying power is angular — apparent size versus naked-eye size at the near point.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: mirror/lens: 1/f = 1/v ± 1/u · maker: 1/f = (μ−1)(1/R₁−1/R₂) · μ = sin[(A+δm)/2]/sin(A/2) · microscope: M = (v₀/u₀)(1 + D/f_e) ≈ −(L/f₀)(1 + D/f_e) · telescope: M = −f₀/f_e, tube length f₀ + f_e (normal adjustment)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Paraxial rays and thin elements throughout; sign conventions fixed once per solution. Microscope formula needs the intermediate image inside the eyepiece focal length (virtual final image at D for relaxed viewing, or at infinity for normal adjustment). Telescope normal adjustment puts the final image at infinity (parallel emergent beam).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Simple microscope (loupe): M = 1 + D/f, object inside f. Compound: objective f₀ ~ mm, eyepiece f_e ~ cm — short tube, huge M. Astronomical: f₀ long, image inverted (fine for stars); terrestrial adds an erecting lens. Combination power adds in contact (P = P₁ + P₂).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Telescope with f₀ = 100 cm, f_e = 5 cm: M = −f₀/f_e = −20×, tube = 105 cm in normal adjustment. Microscope check: L = 16 cm tube, f₀ = 1 cm, f_e = 5 cm, D = 25 cm → M ≈ −(16/1)(1 + 25/5) = −96× — two stages multiply.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Magnification without resolution is empty enlargement — wave optics caps useful M (~1000×, oil immersion). Aberrations (chromatic, spherical) blur real instruments; ray optics cannot explain them away. Reflecting telescopes dodge chromatic error with mirrors instead of lenses.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Microscope: objective gives linear m₀ = v₀/u₀ ≈ L/f₀ (image near tube length L away); eyepiece as loupe multiplies by (1 + D/f_e) → total M product. Telescope: objective forms the image at its focus (parallel incoming beam), eyepiece views it under angle ≈ h/f_e vs naked-eye h/f₀ → M = −f₀/f_e.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Instrument questions: identify objective vs eyepiece roles first, then multiply stages. 'Normal adjustment' = final image at infinity. Prism/lens/mirror sub-parts reuse Class 11 formulas verbatim — the unit is integration, not new laws.
